title: Cavan Sullivan, 16, becomes youngest American goalscorer in Champions Cup history
content:
Philadelphia Union’s Cavan Sullivan, 16, has become the youngest American goalscorer in Champions Cup history.

Sullivan has broken multiple records since signing for the Union in 2024 to the most lucrative homegrown contract in Major League Soccer history. He will join Manchester City when he turns 18.

The midfielder became the youngest player to make his regular-season debut among the top North American professional sports leagues that year, at the age of 14 years and 293 days old. In July, the teenager became MLS’ youngest starter, aged 15.

On Thursday, he scored twice in the Union’s 7-0 win over Defence Force, a top-flight side from Trinidad and Tobago, in the first round of the Champions Cup, as the MLS club secured a 12-0 aggregate victory.

Sullivan scored the Union’s sixth goal in the 76th minute, collecting the ball on the edge of the box, dropping his shoulder to create room for the shot before finding the corner of the net with a left-footed effort from inside the area. It marked his first senior goal for the Union.

He added his side’s second in the 88th minute with a close-range finish after playing an integral role at the beginning of the move. Sullivan picked out team-mate Jesus Bueno with a pass via the outside of his left foot and continued his run into the box, before sliding to turning Sal Olivas’ low delivery into an empty net.

Thursday’s game was his third appearance this season, after coming off the bench in his side’s loss to DC United in the weekend’s MLS opener. He also appeared as a substitute in the first-leg win over Defence Force.

The Champions Cup is a domestic cup competition run by Concacaf, consisting of clubs from across North America, Central America, and the Caribbean. The tournament began in 1962 and the winners qualify for the Club World Cup.

Sullivan made 13 appearances last season as the Union finished top of the Eastern Conference, coming on as a substitute in the semi-final loss to New York City.

The United States youth international went to the Under-17 World Cup that November, registering two goals and two assists over four games. He has represented the U.S at under-15 level as well, leading the side to the 2023 CONCACAF U-15 Championship and earning the player of the tournament award in the process.
